newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian government wins narrow reform victory.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian government wins narrow reform victory.

text.p: The Brazilian government won a narrow but crucial victory in Congress on Wednesday when the Chamber of Deputies approved a controversial bill to reform the civil service.
The bill was approved by 309 members of the lower house, just one vote more than the three-fifths majority it required as a constitutional amendment.
"This legislation will be the salvation of many state and municipal governments which are so bankrupt they can't even pay their staff," political affairs minister Luiz Carlos Santos told reporters.

The reform will allow state and city governments, many of which spend virtually all their receipts on payrolls, to fire workers whose jobs are currently protected by the constitution. The bill also sets a ceiling on pay and pensions for civil servants.

The legislation is considered essential to the long-term prospects of the goverment's economic programme which has slashed Brazil's once-rampant inflation but has so far failed to tackle a stubborn public-sector fiscal deficit, which came in at 3.89 percent of gross domestic product last year.
Government officials say the reform will reduce spending on pay and pensions by $18 billion over the next five years. Brazil currently spends about $100 billion a year on its public sector employees.

The bill ran into fierce resistance, first from trade unions representing public sector workers and then from lawmakers who receive handsome pensions from previous civil service jobs and who stand to lose out under the pay ceiling.

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, fearing defeat, accepted a last-minute compromise in the form of an amendment to the bill exempting members of Congress, ministers and the personal aides of senior civil servants from the pay ceiling.
